channel.title: Aggregated External AI & Tech News
channel.description: Merged headlines from configured external sources

item.title: PeopleSoft 0-day affecting hundreds of organizations steals gigabytes of data (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: Vulnerability in the Oracle-owned PeopleSoft software is about as critical as they come.

item.title: Users cry foul after AMD stripped memory crypto from its consumer CPUs (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: AMD's stripping of TSME from consumer CPUs appears to be a deliberate, covert move.

item.title: Critical Copilot vulnerability allowed hackers to steal 2FA code from users (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: SearchLeak exploit shows why the industry's approach to LLM security fails over and over.

item.title: Year of free HPE software a "step in the correct direction" in VMware rivalry (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: Partner tells Ars that HPE should be giving out more free VM Essentials licenses.

item.title: Windows and Linux users: The deadline to update Secure Boot keys is near (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: What you need to know about the expiration of keys securing your machine's boot sequence.

item.title: "Dangerous" AI models are coming no matter what (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: AI models with advanced hacking capabilities will soon be the norm.

item.title: Tesco moving 40,000 server workloads off VMware amid Broadcom's "abusive conduct" (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: Tesco claimed Broadcom hiked its VMware prices by about 175 percent in UK court filings.

item.title: Massive breach spills credentials for thousands of sensitive networks (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: The affected include Oracle, Lenovo, FedEx, a NATO contractor, and Fortinet.

item.title: Before SpaceX IPO, investors in China secretly acquired stakes (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: One previously unreported SpaceX investor has ties to Chinese military contractors.

item.title: Apple patches high-severity eavesdropping vulnerability in Beats Studio Buds (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: The vulnerability, disclosed 12 months ago, affects multiple manufacturers.

item.title: Microsoft discovers new lightweight backdoor that steals cryptocurrency (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: Crypto Clipper spreads over USB and communicates over Tor.

item.title: Following user outcry, AMD reinstates memory encryption in consumer CPUs (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: Critics saw the move as an underhanded way to steer them toward more costly chips.

item.title: Oracle's 21,000 layoffs help drive its debt-fueled AI investments (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: Oracle is spending billions on data center infrastructure to support AI.

item.title: White House drastically shortens deadline for dropping quantum-vulnerable crypto (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: Order warns of national security risks if post-quantum cryptography isn't adopted in time.

item.title: One-two punch delivered in global operation disrupts cybercrime "assembly line" (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: "Operation Endgame" simultaneously disrupts two widely used crime tools.

item.title: Notion killing Skiff-influenced email app since most users use AI agents instead (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: Notion is "going all in on using agents to run your inbox."

item.title: US offers $10 million for info on group behind Signal and WhatsApp hacking spree (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: Operation by two Russia-state groups has been ongoing since at least March.

item.title: New attack provides one more reason why AI browsers are a bad idea (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: Telling an LLM that 2 + 2 = 5 is enough to make it follow forbidden instructions.

item.title: T-Mobile moving tens of thousands of virtual machines off VMware amid lawsuit (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: T-Mobile wants Broadcom to keep supporting its VMware perpetual licenses.

item.title: Newly discovered PamStealer isn't your typical macOS malware (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: The discovery underscores the increased effort being poured into Mac infostealers.
